opening.text: You never see the foundation of a house. It sits under the floor, out of sight. But everything rests on it. When a storm hits, the walls hold because the foundation holds.
A good father is often like that. His work is quiet and often unseen. But the family stands on it.

mainMessage.text: Fathers matter. They are not extra. They give a family steadiness through love, sacrifice and example. And they are never alone in the work, because God is the perfect Father.

blocks.text: **No one else can fill the space.** A foundation has one job, and no other part of the house can do it. A father has a place in the family that no one else can fill in the same way.
And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
We believe that far from being superfluous, fathers are unique and irreplaceable.
The foundation cannot be swapped out.
**The perfect pattern.** Builders work from a plan. Fathers have one too. Heavenly Father is the perfect example of what a father can be.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The perfect, divine expression of fatherhood is our Heavenly Father.
We build from His plan.
**It costs something.** Laying a foundation is hard, heavy work. Fatherhood asks for time, effort and sacrifice. But it gives back a joy few things can match.

And ye will not suffer your children that they go hungry, or naked; neither will ye suffer that they transgress the laws of God, and fight and quarrel one with another, and serve the devil, who is the master of sin, or who is the evil spirit which hath been spoken of by our fathers, he being an enemy to all righteousness. But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Fatherhood requires sacrifice, but it is a source of incomparable satisfaction, even joy.
The cost is real, and so is the joy.
**Build for the long run.** A good foundation is poured with the future in mind. A father’s task is to raise children in light and truth, even when it means giving up something he wants.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
You are to devote, even sacrifice, yourself to the bringing up of your children in light and truth.
We build for the long run.
**Set the direction.** A house is built facing a certain way. A father helps set the direction of his family. The best direction is toward the Church, the covenants and the ordinances.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Lead your family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances.
The house faces the right way.
**Show, do not just tell.** Children do not read the foundation. They live in the house. A father’s example is what they feel every day. They need a model.
The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The Lord expects fathers to help shape their children, and children want and need a model.
Children live on what we model.

story.title: Abraham Teaches His Household

blocks.text: The Lord knew Abraham. He knew that Abraham would teach his family to follow Him.

For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.
Abraham’s teaching reached his household and beyond.

opening.text: A good coach does not play the game for the team. He prepares them. He teaches the basics, runs the drills and stands at the sideline. When a player makes a mistake, the coach does not walk off. He stays and helps.
That is a lot like what a father can be. He cannot live his children’s lives for them. But he can stand beside them, teach them and cheer them on.

mainMessage.text: A father coaches by loving, teaching and showing the way. It costs him time and effort. But it brings deep joy, and he is guided by the perfect Father.

blocks.text: **There is only one coach for this team.** A team might have many helpers, but its own coach is special. A father is unique and irreplaceable in his family.
And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
We believe that far from being superfluous, fathers are unique and irreplaceable.
No one else can be his coach.
**Learn from the best.** Great coaches learn from great coaches. A father learns from his Heavenly Father, who is the perfect model of love and patience.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The perfect, divine expression of fatherhood is our Heavenly Father.
We learn from the Best.
**Early mornings and late nights.** Coaching takes more time than anyone sees. Fatherhood does too. It asks a lot, and it gives back something worth more than the cost.

And ye will not suffer your children that they go hungry, or naked; neither will ye suffer that they transgress the laws of God, and fight and quarrel one with another, and serve the devil, who is the master of sin, or who is the evil spirit which hath been spoken of by our fathers, he being an enemy to all righteousness. But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Fatherhood requires sacrifice, but it is a source of incomparable satisfaction, even joy.
The effort pays back in joy.
**Teach them the real game.** The real game is raising children to know God. A father gives his best for that, even when it costs him something he would like to keep.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
You are to devote, even sacrifice, yourself to the bringing up of your children in light and truth.
The real game is raising children in light.
**Call the play.** A coach picks a direction. A father leads his family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances. That is the game plan that matters most.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Lead your family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances.
That is the play that matters.
**Players watch the coach.** Young players copy what they see. If the coach stays calm, they learn calm. A father’s example shapes his children more than his speeches.
The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The Lord expects fathers to help shape their children, and children want and need a model.
They learn from what they see.

story.title: The Father of the Prodigal Son

blocks.text: A young man left home and made poor choices. When he finally turned back, his father saw him from far away.
And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The father had been watching and waiting. A good father never gives up on a child.

application.text: First, pick one child, or one young person you care about, and ask about their day. Then really listen.
Second, share one lesson you learned the hard way.
Third, if a relationship with a child feels broken, speak with your bishop or branch president. Help is available.

opening.text: A big tree stands through wind and snow. What you see is the trunk and the leaves. What you do not see are the roots. They go deep and spread wide. They take in water and hold the tree to the ground. Without them, the first storm would knock it over.
A father can be like the roots of a family. His work is often out of sight. But it holds everything in place.

mainMessage.text: A father helps a family stay rooted. He does it through steady love, sacrifice and example. He is guided by the perfect Father, and he leads his family toward God.

blocks.text: **One set of roots.** A tree cannot borrow roots from another tree. A family cannot borrow a father. His place is his own, and no one can take it.
And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
We believe that far from being superfluous, fathers are unique and irreplaceable.
His place is his own.
**Roots reach for water.** Roots go where the water is. A father goes to the source too. Heavenly Father is the perfect example, and fathers can draw from Him.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The perfect, divine expression of fatherhood is our Heavenly Father.
We draw from the source.
**Roots work hard.** Pushing through hard ground takes effort. Fatherhood takes effort too. But what grows is a source of deep joy.

And ye will not suffer your children that they go hungry, or naked; neither will ye suffer that they transgress the laws of God, and fight and quarrel one with another, and serve the devil, who is the master of sin, or who is the evil spirit which hath been spoken of by our fathers, he being an enemy to all righteousness. But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Fatherhood requires sacrifice, but it is a source of incomparable satisfaction, even joy.
The work is hard, and the joy is deep.
**Feed the branches.** Roots send life up to every branch. A father gives his best so his children can grow in light and truth.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
You are to devote, even sacrifice, yourself to the bringing up of your children in light and truth.
He gives so they can grow.
**Grow toward the light.** Trees lean toward the sun. A father can lean his family toward the Lord, toward the Church, the covenants and the ordinances.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Lead your family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances.
He leans the family toward the light.
**Young trees learn from old ones.** Seedlings grow near older trees and take shape from them. Children do that with their fathers. They need an example to follow.
The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The Lord expects fathers to help shape their children, and children want and need a model.
Children take shape from the example.

story.title: Joseph Protects His Family

blocks.text: An angel warned Joseph that the child Jesus was in danger. Joseph did not wait. He took his family and left at once, in the night.

And when they were departed, behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him. When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.
Joseph listened and acted. A father who follows God’s guidance protects his family.

opening.text: Every set of stairs has a handrail. You do not think about it much. You hold it when the steps are steep. A child grabs it without being told. An older person leans on it. It does not move or complain. It is just there.
A father can be that kind of steady support for his family.

mainMessage.text: A good father is a steady handrail. He holds firm so others can climb. He learns from Heavenly Father, gives of himself and leads the way to the Lord.

blocks.text: **Built in, not added on.** A handrail is part of the staircase. A father is part of the family. He is unique and cannot be replaced.
And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
We believe that far from being superfluous, fathers are unique and irreplaceable.
He is part of the staircase.
**Anchored in something strong.** A handrail is only as good as what holds it. A father is anchored to his Heavenly Father, who is the perfect model.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The perfect, divine expression of fatherhood is our Heavenly Father.

And ye will not suffer your children that they go hungry, or naked; neither will ye suffer that they transgress the laws of God, and fight and quarrel one with another, and serve the devil, who is the master of sin, or who is the evil spirit which hath been spoken of by our fathers, he being an enemy to all righteousness. But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Fatherhood requires sacrifice, but it is a source of incomparable satisfaction, even joy.
He carries the weight, and finds joy in it.
**It goes all the way up.** A good handrail does not stop halfway. A father’s care for his children goes all the way, even when it costs him something he would like to keep.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
You are to devote, even sacrifice, yourself to the bringing up of your children in light and truth.
His care goes all the way.
**It leads somewhere.** A handrail shows which way is up. A father points his family toward the Church, the covenants and the ordinances.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Lead your family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances.
It shows the way up.
**Children copy the grip.** A child watches how others hold the rail. In time, they hold it the same way. Children hold on to what their father models.
The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The Lord expects fathers to help shape their children, and children want and need a model.
They hold what he models.

story.title: Lehi Wants His Family to Partake

blocks.text: Lehi had a vision of the tree of life. The fruit filled him with joy. His first thought was of his family.

And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit. And as I cast my eyes round about, that perhaps I might discover my family also, I beheld a river of water; and it ran along, and it was near the tree of which I was partaking the fruit.
A good father wants his family to share in what is best.

application.text: First, think of something good in your life that you want your family to share. Plan a way to share it.

Third, if you feel unsure about your place in your family, speak with your bishop or branch president.

opening.text: On a dark path, one person carries a lantern. The light is small. It does not light the whole forest. But it shows the next few steps, and everyone behind it can see where to put their feet.
A father can be that lantern bearer for his family. He may not see the whole road. But he can carry the light and walk ahead.

mainMessage.text: A father carries the light for his family. He learns from Heavenly Father, gives his time and strength, and walks toward the Lord. His children follow the light they see in him.

blocks.text: **One lantern, one bearer.** Each family has one father, and no one else can carry that lantern. His place is unique and cannot be replaced.
And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
We believe that far from being superfluous, fathers are unique and irreplaceable.
His lantern lights his family.
**Lit from a greater fire.** The lantern is lit from another flame. A father is lit by Heavenly Father, the perfect example of fatherhood.

The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The perfect, divine expression of fatherhood is our Heavenly Father.
He is lit from a greater fire.
**Heavy to carry.** A lantern is a weight in the hand, and the path is long. Fatherhood takes sacrifice. But the light on the faces behind him is worth it.

And ye will not suffer your children that they go hungry, or naked; neither will ye suffer that they transgress the laws of God, and fight and quarrel one with another, and serve the devil, who is the master of sin, or who is the evil spirit which hath been spoken of by our fathers, he being an enemy to all righteousness. But ye will teach them to walk in the ways of truth and soberness; ye will teach them to love one another, and to serve one another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Fatherhood requires sacrifice, but it is a source of incomparable satisfaction, even joy.
The weight is worth the light.
**Give the light away.** A good lantern bearer does not keep the light to himself. He gives himself so the children can walk in light and truth.
And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
You are to devote, even sacrifice, yourself to the bringing up of your children in light and truth.
He gives his light away.
**Walk toward the right place.** Light is useful because it leads somewhere. A father leads his family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
Elder Boyd K. Packer, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “The Father and the Family” from the April 1994 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Lead your family to the Church, to the covenants and ordinances.
The light leads somewhere.
**Children step where the light falls.** Children walk where the lantern shows. They follow what they see. Fathers help shape their children by the way they live.
The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Fathers” from the April 2016 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
The Lord expects fathers to help shape their children, and children want and need a model.
They follow the light they see.

story.title: Alma Counsels His Son

blocks.text: Alma gave his son Helaman careful counsel. He wanted him to learn early what Alma had learned the hard way.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
A father’s counsel can light a long road for his child.

application.text: First, write down one thing your father, or a father figure, taught you that you still value. Say thanks to him if you can.
Second, share one piece of good counsel with a young person this week.
